headline: 1 failing test(s) indicate a real implementation bug; human review required

classifications.rationale: The contract requires the round-trip property decode(encode(x)) == x for every string x. The candidate's encode produces 'a111' for input 'a1', which decode expands to 'a' repeated 111 times, violating round-trip. This is a genuine defect in the candidate.
classifications.contract_basis: Contract: 'encode must return a str and must round-trip with decode (decode(encode(x)) == x for every string x).'

classifications.rationale: The test uses string literals '\\n\\n\\t' and '\\n2\\t1', which in Python source represent literal backslash-n sequences (six characters), not newline and tab characters. The contract does not specify this input-output pair; it only requires encode to work for any string, including actual newlines and tabs. The test is defective due to incorrect escaping.
classifications.contract_basis: Contract: 'each maximal run of one character becomes that character followed by the decimal count of the run' - the test does not faithfully encode this for newline/tab.

modules.corrected_notes: One failing test (roundtrip) reveals a genuine implementation bug: the candidate's encode does not satisfy the round-trip property for strings containing digits. The other failing test (newline/tab) is defective due to incorrect string literals in the test. Since not all failing tests are test_defects, corrected_module is null.

note: original tests, results and reasons are preserved unchanged; arbitration is advisory unless apply mode is on, and never flips an implementation bug or contract dispute
